item.title: 2026-11-03 Manitoba & Winnipeg: Sewage Spill, Severance Payouts, and a Mine Fire
item.description: - Nearly 10 million litres of sewage hit the Red River Monday after bypass gates opened unexpectedly. - Nine outgoing councillors are in line for roughly 525 thousand dollars combined in severance. - Thompson's T3 mine had an underground equipment fire Thursday, no injuries, mine back in operation. - Garden Valley School Division is working through a cybersecurity incident affecting its IT systems. - Permanent standard time is still causing scheduling headaches for Manitoba businesses.

item.title: 2026-11-03 Canadian Politics: Budget Preview, Pipeline Fights, and Carney in Antigua
item.description: - Budget Thursday: small business tax relief expected, details still thin. - PBO warns borrowing is outpacing the deficit and debt accounting is less transparent. - Trade talks with Washington set to restart within days. - Carney in Antigua for Commonwealth summit amid US midterms. - Pacific Link pipeline faces growing First Nations court challenges in BC.

item.title: 2026-11-03 Climate Policy & Nonprofit Governance: Budget, Pensions, and Charity Rule Changes
item.description: - Pension funds in LNG Canada draw "indefensible" label from climate groups, watch for client questions. - Parks Canada cuts could slow Jasper's wildfire rebuild, a reputational risk for federal climate credibility. - Ontario's permitting bill cuts appeal rights, a bellwether for provincial deregulation trends. - Carney's Antigua trip tests balancing climate finance asks with trade priorities. - CRA no longer pre-approves charity purpose changes, boards now carry more compliance risk.

item.title: 2026-11-03 AI & Technology: Anthropic's RSI Warning and Europe's Freezer Hacks
item.description: - Anthropic's self-improvement warning means capability timelines could compress faster than compliance timelines. - Second freezer cyberattack in weeks shows industrial control systems are now a real, not hypothetical, target. - No ransom in either attack suggests sabotage motive, which changes the insurance conversation. - Brookfield's twenty-seven billion dollar UK data centre deal shows AI capex spreading beyond chipmakers into utilities. - Marvell's 115 billion dollar Lumentum purchase is another sign networking hardware is the next AI investment front.

item.title: 2026-11-03 Health & Fitness: Short Workouts, Bird Flu, and Early Flu Season
item.description: - Short, frequent strength sessions may match long workouts for building muscle, per new research. - Treat that exercise snacking study as early and small, not a training overhaul. - First US bird flu death since last year, tied to a Washington dairy, public risk still low. - Canada's flu season arrived roughly seven weeks early this year. - Manitoba flu shots have been available since mid-October, worth getting now.

item.title: 2026-11-03 Parenting: Screen Time Harms Mount, Pediatric Guidance Holds
item.description: - Globe and Mail: experts want screens treated as a public health issue for kids. - CPS guidance: zero screens under two, except video calls with family. - Ages two to five: cap routine screen use under one hour daily. - Risk flagged: language, self-regulation, and executive function development. - Good opener with clients who are new parents or grandparents.

item.title: 2026-11-03 Sports: Jets Skid Hits Nine, Raiders Brace For 49ers
item.description: - Jets at nine straight losses, now the NHL's biggest story in Canada. - Raiders face a tough 6-1 Niners team Sunday in the Bay Area. - Kucherov trade request shakes up the NHL landscape. - Lamar Jackson's injury could end his Ravens tenure. - Blue Bombers pulled off a road upset in Toronto.
